9300204.headline: Treaty United Women Ready to Write Final Chapter of Historic 2026 Campaign on Home Turf
9300204.subheadline: Limerick side prepares for emotional season finale against DLR Waves at Markets Field this evening.
9300204.story:
Treaty United’s women’s team is set to bring down the curtain on a landmark SSE Airtricity Premier Division campaign this evening, welcoming DLR Waves to Limerick for a 5pm kickoff. The fixture marks the culmination of months of dedication, growth, and competitive football that has continued to capture the imagination of local sports enthusiasts throughout the region.

As the squad prepares to step onto the pitch for the final time this season, players and coaching staff alike are reflecting on the progress made over the past several months. The team has consistently demonstrated resilience and determination, representing Limerick proudly on the national stage and inspiring the next generation of young players coming through local grassroots clubs across the county.

Supporters are expected to turn out in strong numbers to show their appreciation for the squad's efforts this season. Tonight’s match is not only the final fixture on the calendar but also an opportunity to celebrate a positive trajectory for women's football in the region, paving the way for even greater achievements when the team returns to action in the future.
9300204.pullQuote: The Treaty United women's side is ready to finish their 2026 campaign in style in front of home supporters.

Munster rugby supporters across Limerick and the wider province are turning their attention to the upcoming inter-provincial challenge as preparations ramp up for a high-stakes fixture against Leinster. Following a string of encouraging performances and a decisive 31-14 victory in the corresponding fixture last season, the squad is eager to maintain their upward trajectory in the United Rugby Championship (URC).

Head coach and players have been putting in rigorous work on the training ground, aiming to harness the positive energy from recent outings to deliver another memorable performance for the passionate home faithful. The upcoming match offers an ideal platform for the team to showcase their tactical growth, depth, and resilience against formidable opposition.

For the local community, fixtures against Leinster always carry a special significance, uniting fans in pubs, clubs, and Thomond Park to celebrate the spirit of the game. As the province builds towards kick-off, the collective optimism surrounding the team highlights the enduring connection between Munster Rugby and the people of Limerick, promising an electrifying atmosphere for all in attendance.

9307685.headline: Bank Holiday Bonanza: Lucky Limerick Ticket Holder Claims Half-Million EuroMillions Prize
9307685.subheadline: National Lottery officials urge players across the county to check their numbers following Friday night's massive draw.
9307685.story:
There is a buzz of excitement across the Treaty County this weekend as National Lottery officials confirm that a single ticket holder in Limerick has won a staggering €500,000 in the EuroMillions draw. The life-changing win is expected to set the stage for an unforgettable Bank Holiday weekend for the yet-unnamed lucky participant.

While the exact location where the winning ticket was purchased has not yet been revealed by lottery headquarters, anticipation is already building in local shops and communities. National Lottery spokesperson Emma Monaghan shared the thrilling news on Saturday morning, encouraging everyone who participated in Friday's draw to thoroughly check their slips.

"There could be a very exciting Bank Holiday weekend ahead for one EuroMillions player in Limerick who is now holding a €500,000 winning ticket," Monaghan said, urging the winner to sign the back of their ticket, keep it safe, and contact the National Lottery prize claims team to arrange collecting their substantial sum.

As celebrations begin to unfold across the region, this latest win brings a welcome dose of joy and optimism to the local community. It serves as a timely reminder of the exciting possibilities that await players right here in Limerick, adding an extra layer of festive cheer to the long weekend festivities.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362473.headline: Council Trials Innovative 'Zero Gravity' Mower to Boost Limerick's Biodiversity and Cut Emissions
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362473.subheadline: New machinery trial paves the way for sustainable meadow management across the county.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362473.story:
Limerick City and County Council has successfully completed a trial of an advanced 'zero gravity' mowing system designed to enhance local biodiversity and support the county's climate action objectives. The specialized GHS Drive 1800 machine was leased for a pilot program focusing on grasslands and pollinator-friendly meadows within the Limerick Decarbonisation Zone and surrounding areas.

Unlike traditional mowing equipment, the innovative machine cuts and removes vegetation in a single, highly efficient operation. Environmental experts emphasize that removing grass cuttings is a vital best-practice technique for meadow management, as it reduces soil fertility and creates the optimal conditions for native wildflowers and pollinators to thrive. The successful trial aligns directly with the local authority's commitments under the Limerick Biodiversity Action Plan, the Climate Action Plan, and the All-Ireland Pollinator Plan.

Beyond its ecological benefits, the pilot highlighted significant operational advantages for the local authority. The machinery demonstrated reduced fuel consumption, lower greenhouse gas emissions, and a quieter operation compared to conventional equipment. Furthermore, research indicates that properly managed wildflower meadows encourage deeper root systems and increased soil carbon storage, gradually transforming local green spaces into valuable carbon sinks.

Building on the positive outcomes of the lease program, Limerick City and County Council is now exploring the permanent acquisition of similar technology. The move marks another proactive step in the region's long-term approach to sustainable open space management, ensuring that Limerick continues to lead by example in local environmental stewardship.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362473.pullQuote: Removing cuttings from meadows is recognised as a best-practice management technique, creating the conditions needed for a greater diversity of native wildflowers and pollinators to thrive.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362473.localAngle: The trial of the zero-gravity mower within the Limerick Decarbonisation Zone demonstrates the local authority's ongoing commitment to meeting county-wide climate action and biodiversity targets.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362473.originalTitle: Zero gravity machine hitting heights in biodiversity

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362470.headline: Abbeyfeale Property Transfer Sparks Healthy Debate on Local Development Strategy
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362470.subheadline: Elected members weigh in on proposed housing initiative involving Limerick Twenty Thirty
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362470.story:
Elected representatives in West Limerick are engaging in constructive discussions regarding a visionary proposal to allocate six council-owned properties in Abbeyfeale to Limerick Twenty Thirty. Unveiled at the October Newcastle West district meeting, the initiative aims to breathe new life into local housing stock, offering a sustainable, cost-recovery rental model tailored for working households and key workers in the area.

The properties—located at Convent Road, Colbert Terrace, Old Church Street, and the Bridge Inn—include a mix of one, two, three, and four-bedroom homes. Refurbished to an exceptionally high standard, these Grade A residences are expected to be ready by mid-November. Supporters of the project, including District Cathaoirleach Cllr Liam Galvin, highlight that bringing these previously idle buildings back into active use addresses a long-standing community priority and will significantly strengthen local spending power and economic sustainability in West Limerick.

At the same time, councillors are proactively examining the broader implications of utilizing a project development company traditionally focused on commercial growth for residential schemes. Fianna Fáil councillor Michael Collins raised important questions during the district meeting regarding the distinction between commercial and private housing mandates, calling for a dedicated workshop to ensure all elected members can collaborate on the optimal path forward. District leaders remain committed to open dialogue, balancing the urgent need to activate local housing with strategic planning for the county's long-term commercial vitality.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362470.pullQuote: I believe we will have them ready by the middle of November. I wasn’t 100 per cent in favour of the scheme that the Mayor was proposing but I am willing to give it a chance.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362470.localAngle: The proposed disposal of Abbeyfeale council properties to Limerick Twenty Thirty marks a pivotal step in shaping the future of housing and economic development across West Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362470.originalTitle: Proposed disposal of Abbeyfeale properties to Limerick Twenty Thirty raises serious questions

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362466.headline: Limerick Property Market Shows Steady Growth with Rising Inventory and Slower Inflation Rates
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362466.subheadline: Latest MyHome report highlights positive trends for local homebuyers as market supply improves across the county.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362466.story:
Property prices in Limerick have seen a steady annual increase of €10,000, bringing the median asking price across the county to €290,000, according to the latest MyHome Property Price Report for the third quarter of 2026. While the figures reflect continuous growth over the past year, asking prices remained flat over the final quarter, pointing to a stabilizing market environment for local buyers and sellers alike.

Specific property categories across the county have experienced varied shifts. Asking prices for three-bed semi-detached homes rose by €15,000 over the past year to reach €295,000, which includes a modest €5,000 increase in the third quarter alone. Meanwhile, four-bed semi-detached houses saw a decrease of €5,500 annually to settle at a median asking price of €359,500, despite experiencing a €7,000 rise during the most recent quarter. Market activity has also seen encouraging improvements, with 444 properties listed for sale in Limerick at the close of the third quarter—marking a 4 per cent increase over the period. Properties are currently going sale agreed in just under three months on average.

Industry experts have welcomed these developments as encouraging signs for the local housing market. Conall MacCoille, Chief Economist at Bank of Ireland, highlighted that the slowing rate of asking price inflation, combined with an increasing number of properties for sale and a pickup in homebuilding, creates a more favorable environment for prospective buyers. Additionally, MyHome Managing Director Joanne Geary pointed to strong engagement from first-time buyers, noting that first-time buyer transactions have risen by 12 per cent year-on-year, reflecting continued confidence and accessibility in Limerick's property sector.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362466.pullQuote: The rate of asking price inflation continues to slow, the number of properties for sale on MyHome is rising, and homebuilding has picked up.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362466.localAngle: The latest MyHome Property Price Report provides local readers with a comprehensive look at median asking prices, inventory levels, and housing market trends across Limerick county.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362466.originalTitle: Limerick property prices continue to rise according to new report

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362391.headline: Terror and Talent Set for the Belltable as 'Big Shots Halloween Screams' Returns to Limerick
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362391.subheadline: Ireland's premier all-island horror film competition is back on Treaty City screens this Halloween night with original short films, live audiences, and cash prizes.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362391.story:
Film enthusiasts and horror fans across Limerick are in for a spine-chilling treat next weekend as the Belltable prepares to host the return of 'Big Shots Halloween Screams' on Saturday, October 31. Following successful runs in 2024 and 2025, Ireland’s All-Island Horror Film Competition is once again bringing its unique brand of cinematic terror to the heart of the city, offering local audiences a front-row seat to some of the freshest talent in independent filmmaking.

Throughout the month of October, creative teams from every corner of the island have been hard at work writing, shooting, and editing their own original short horror films. These homegrown productions will culminate in a special live screening event at the Belltable, where audiences can experience the suspense together on the big screen. In addition to the thrill of the premiere, participating filmmakers will be competing for a range of prestigious awards and cash prizes.

Doors for the Halloween night event will open at 6.30pm, with the screenings set to kick off at 7.30pm. Tickets are available now for €12.50, offering an affordable and entertaining evening out for local culture seekers and horror aficionados alike. As cultural events continue to thrive in Limerick, the return of Big Shots Halloween Screams highlights the city's vibrant arts community and provides an exciting platform for emerging cinematic storytellers to showcase their craft.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362391.pullQuote: Teams from across the island will write, shoot and edit original short horror films throughout October for the live Belltable screening.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362391.localAngle: The popular all-island horror film competition returns to Limerick's Belltable venue, offering local film fans a thrilling Halloween night out.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362391.originalTitle: Big Shots Halloween Screams returns to Belltable for another night of frights

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362371.headline: Youth-Led LASTA ‘26 Festival Brings Fresh Energy and Creativity to the Belltable Stage
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362371.subheadline: Co-curators Marcus Cropper and Ilinca Luca invite Limerick audiences to celebrate young artistic talent in a dynamic two-event programme.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362371.story:
The Belltable is set to come alive with youthful creativity and vibrant performances later this month as it hosts LASTA ‘26, a nationwide festival spearheaded by the Young Curators national mentorship programme. Local culture enthusiasts and young audiences alike are in for a treat as co-curators Marcus Cropper and Ilinca Luca unveil a diverse programme designed to transform the iconic Limerick venue into a welcoming space for artistic experimentation and community connection.

The festival kicks off on Wednesday, October 28, with two screenings of the timeless workplace comedy 9 to 5, scheduled for 5pm and 7.30pm. Presented personally by Ms. Luca and Mr. Cropper, the screenings serve as a special tribute to the legendary 1980 film starring Dolly Parton, Lily Tomlin, and Jane Fonda. Tickets for the cinematic event are affordably priced at €8 general admission and €5 concession, offering an accessible evening out for film fans across the city.

The excitement continues on Friday, October 30, at 7.30pm with 'Nighttime Medley', an intimate variety show that promises an unforgettable evening of performance, drag clowning, and contemporary dance. Billed as a celebration of mischief-makers and bold artistry, the line-up features acclaimed Limerick-based dance artist Alex Vostokova—an Associate Artist at Dance Limerick—alongside Dublin-based performer Day Magee and rising drag clown sensation Whimsy. Ms. Vostokova will present her thought-provoking piece Pit, commissioned by Coisceim Dance Theatre, which explores the impact of modern urbanism through powerful choreography.

Events like LASTA ‘26 highlight the vital role that young people play in shaping Limerick’s vibrant cultural landscape. By providing a platform for emerging artists and welcoming peers into the heart of the city's arts scene, the festival reinforces the Belltable's position as a dynamic hub for community engagement, inspiration, and creative expression.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362371.pullQuote: Co-curators Marcus Cropper and Ilinca Luca have put together a programme that welcomes their peers into the venue as a space for creative experimentation and fun.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362371.localAngle: Limerick-based dance artist Alex Vostokova will perform her acclaimed piece 'Pit' at the Belltable as part of the nationwide LASTA '26 festival.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362371.originalTitle: Young curators bring LASTA ‘26 to Belltable with film screening and variety show
